title: Becoming an ADI: Parts 1, 2, 3 & the Register
whatItIs: To join the ADI register you pass 3 tests: theory (part 1), driving ability (part 2) and instructional ability (part 3), all within 2 years of passing part 1.
keyFacts: Start with a new DBS check. Parts 2 and 3 must be passed within 2 years of passing part 1.
You get 3 attempts each at parts 2 and 3.
Part 3 grades: 31 to 42 = grade B, 43 to 51 = grade A.
After passing part 3, apply for your first ADI badge within 12 months, or take all 3 tests again.
Renew your registration and DBS check every 4 years, with at least one standards check every 4 years.

a.label: Trainee licence (pink badge)
points: After part 2 and 40 hours' training; lasts 6 months
20% of lessons supervised, or at least 20 hours' extra training

onTheTest.question: On ADI part 3 a trainee scores 33 overall but only 7 in the risk management category. What is the result?
options: Fail: 7 or less in risk management is an automatic fail
Fail, because the total is below 43
onTheTest.why: Scoring 7 or less in risk management is an automatic fail, whatever the total. Otherwise 31 to 42 would be grade B.

onTheTest.question: A trainee licence holder chooses option 1 (supervision). What must they do?
options: Be supervised for every lesson they give
Be supervised for 40 hours in total
Do 20 hours of extra training within 6 months
Be supervised by their sponsoring ADI for 20% of all lessons
onTheTest.why: Option 1 is supervision by the sponsoring ADI for 20% of all lessons given, recorded on form ADI 21S. Option 2 is at least 20 hours of extra training.

traps: Part 2 eyesight is 27 m (27.5 m old-style), not 20 m, and failing it uses one of the 3 attempts.
It is illegal to give paid lessons after failing part 3 for the third time.
An ADI must tell DVSA in writing within 7 days of any caution or conviction, including penalty points.
Trainees must advertise as 'trainee driving instructor', not 'PDI', and give only the school's contact details.
